body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Friday, August 21, 2026, and we’re starting the day with a high near 101° and air quality at a moderate 71. Overnight, a semi truck fully engulfed on northbound I-5 south of Grapevine kept crews busy well into the morning, and a fast-moving brush fire on McCombs Road north of Wasco drew a heavy response. Today’s top story is a look at how the Mission of Kern is shifting its approach to homelessness with a treatment-first recovery model. Let’s get you caught up.

## The Kern Overnight

The night’s most significant incident unfolded just before 1 a.m. when a semi truck with a trailer became fully engulfed on the number three lane of northbound I-5 south of Grapevine. CHP and Engine 56 were on scene, and command was established as the Tejon Incident. Crews worked the fire for hours; by 6 a.m., they were still on site, a heavy-duty tow had been called in, and traffic was backing up to the Lebec service route. Earlier in the evening, around 10:34 p.m., a quarter-acre brush fire on McCombs Road (State Route 43 north of Wasco) was burning with a fast rate of spread and potential to run west. Multiple engines and a water tender responded, and additional wildland equipment was ordered for what command described as a lengthy mop-up. In north Bakersfield, an armed robbery was reported around 9:50 p.m. on Denise Avenue, with the suspect described as a transient white male in his late 30s wearing a baseball cap and black face mask, pulling a wagon, and accompanied by a white female. Around 3 a.m., two subjects were on a Woodford Boulevard property behind a white pickup, possibly taking items; the subjects were known to be in possession of firearms, though none were visible at first, and officers later made contact and located a firearm. The night closed out with a foot pursuit at a trucking yard south of Gibson Street around 4:36 a.m. after three subjects were reported possibly taking items. Deputies set a perimeter, and the subjects ran—one headed south toward a fence with an officer holding the hole. One subject was described as known to carry a knife.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 101° and a low around 73° tonight. It’s currently 77° at Meadows Field (KBFL). There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, and air quality is moderate at an AQI of 71. Conditions should remain clear and warm throughout the day.

## Top stories

**According to 23ABC, the Mission of Kern is shifting its approach to homelessness by adopting a treatment-first recovery model.** Homelessness in Kern County increased by 3.2% from 2025 to 2026, and shelters like the Mission of Kern are responding with a new strategy that prioritizes drug treatment for unhoused residents to help them gain clarity before considering broader financial considerations, such as their housing situation. The White House approved a new homeless addiction recovery plan last Wednesday that highlights this approach. James Copley, a recovery advocate, shares his personal story of lasting sobriety, crediting programs like the one at the Mission of Kern. Carlos Baldovinos, the executive director of the Mission of Kern, notes that every person who comes through the doors faces a unique set of challenges, and advocates believe helping people heal from the inside out is key to keeping them from returning to the streets.

**KGET 17 reports that Kern County leaders are set to vote on a support letter expressing frustration toward California policies.** The letter, which some are calling a “two-state solution” support letter, reflects the county’s growing dissatisfaction with state-level decisions. The vote is expected to take place at an upcoming meeting, and the discussion is likely to center on how these policies are affecting local governance and community well-being. This move comes amid a broader conversation in Kern County about the balance of power between local and state authorities.

**Bakersfield Now tells us that a 32-year-old Bakersfield man has died of dehydration tied to heat exposure.** The Kern County Coroner’s Office has identified the man, and an investigation into the circumstances surrounding his death is ongoing. This tragic incident serves as a reminder of the dangers posed by extreme heat, especially as temperatures in our area continue to rise. Residents are encouraged to stay hydrated and take precautions when spending time outdoors.

## Something good

In a heartening piece of news, **23ABC shares that a Foothill High School graduate has won a $25,000 scholarship to attend his dream school.** Eric Ventura was awarded the California Table Grape Scholarship after applying last October. After months of waiting, he learned he won the $25,000 award, which will be spread across his four years at UC Berkeley. Ventura credits the nonprofit Youth 2 Leaders with helping him and his parents navigate the process, and he knows what hard work looks like—his summer breaks typically included waking up early to work in the fields alongside his family. UC Berkeley has been Ventura’s dream school since he first visited on a field trip with Youth 2 Leaders, and this scholarship will help make that dream a reality.

## Coming up this week

Looking ahead, the Fox Theater has a full lineup of events starting this weekend. On Saturday, August 22, Los Yonic’s Zamacona, Los Caminantes, and Grupo Yndio will take the stage. Then on Tuesday, August 25, the Cults & Classics: Season Pass 2026-2027 goes on sale. Later in the week, Rodney Carrington performs on Thursday, August 27, followed by CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE on Friday, August 28. Willie Barcena takes the stage on Saturday, August 29, and that same evening, the Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix will be held. On the civic front, the City Council will hold two meetings on Wednesday, August 26—one at 3:30 p.m. and another at 5:15 p.m. These meetings are open to the public, and residents are encouraged to attend and participate in local governance.
